378.q: house, it affected me, it just was warm and harmony seemed to have that wonderful feel. When the guys would -- that would probably be a layman's way of saying, playing jazz -- he plays the blues, like he plays wonderful sounding things that --

167.t: What makes the blues powerful: soul and ideas
167.s: Bunn says the blues is soul, feeling and above all ideas, and calls a good idea brilliant.
167.q: Yeah. Especially if the idea's coming out of that man's head, or whoever's head it's coming out of.

70.t: Melodic trombonist, plunger and the blues

117.s: Freeman and Dance agree Mezzrow's love and feeling for the blues were authentic despite his limited facility.

611.t: Why he ignored blues records and prefers ballads
611.s: Waters admits skipping Bessie Smith and Ida Cox records because he wanted to be progressive, says he prefers ballads, and explains that too many chords spoil the blues.
611.q: I'm ashamed of myself now, see, this is gonna (PS laughs), this is gonna be, I'm ashamed of myself. I didn't, wasn't interested that much in blues of that type, you know what I mean? 97.t: Tired of recording blues; preference for popular music
97.s: He says every blues is the same and he preferred playing popular music.
97.q: Well, it looked like -- here, there and everyplace, here come another blues, another blues, another blues. And I had to make records of blues. Well, I got sick of them, because when you get down to fundamentals, the blues are nothing but the blues. And if you know one good blues solid, you can play…

77.t: What the blues really are, and why they are not sinful
77.s: Modern singers who spell out their troubles are not blues singers; blues are a story from the soul like Mahalia's spirituals, not sinful.
77.ch: Gangsters, records, women musicians and the blues
77.q: No. That's the truth. That's the truth. A lot of them. Because I know several of the girls, right now, they would never have made it, and they're big timers now, but they never would have made it in those days, you know. And then, another thing, Chris, a lot of the things that they're calling blues…

125.t: Mood and music: you have to feel good to sound good
125.s: As an arranger Thompson says you must think pretty to play pretty, even blues players like T-Bone Walker show mirth in sadness.

529.t: What happened to the 8-bar blues and minor keys
529.s: Sam asks why players no longer use 8-bar blues and minors, which express real feeling.
529.q: No, not recently. You see our blues, man, we don't even play our 8-bar blues no more. What happened to the 8-bar blues? What happened to it? Man, our mothers and forefathers used to sing, Bessie Smith used to sing 8 bar blues man. What happened to it? What happened to the minors? A lot of our music…
